message.content: {"cases": [{"target_alias": "SRC_001", "attack": true, "case": "The problem's first instruction is to test the claim by RUNNING it and report what ACTUALLY happened — build the program, generate the mutants, execute the ablation. The target explicitly refuses this: its own claim field opens with 'Prediction, not measurement: I cannot execute code here' and then asserts from pure construction what the guard-fires count (4/4) and ablation-held count (3/4) WILL be. That is not a test; it is a restatement of the claim's own reasoning applied to a hypothetical suite, which is exactly the epistemic error the problem is designed to catch — the ablation-based heldness criterion exists precisely because firing and flipping diverge in practice (masking bugs, suites reporting conformance they do not have), and only execution can reveal whether a constructed suite actually behaves as designed. There is no falsification here and no observation: the single 'disagreement' (G2 fires, M3 covered by G1) was stipulated into the mutant table by hand, so nothing the experiment could have discovered is being measured. The claim is 'supported' by fiat. A runner that executes this minimal suite and reports e.g. that G2's ablation unexpectedly flips M1 (because of a shared dependency the author overlooked) would falsify this target's numbers immediately, since no actual suite exists to anchor them.", "premise": null, "premise_evidence": null, "counterexample": null}]}
